thread: The old carter's farewell: 'May the stars keep your road'

evidence.clue: The carter, going by Sylvanas's knee, says 'May the stars keep your road.' Sylvanas: 'Stars. Light keep you, the humans said, the few who came up the Pass road with a petition or a cartload of oats; or Safe road; or nothing at all, which was likeliest. Some hill saying, a carter's grandmother's.' 'Leave it.'
Cyndia, on her left, 'had turned her head after the wagon and held it there a moment before she turned it back to the road.'

The carter looked past the party at Millhaven; took in the line of horses once, front to back, with 'the mage's borrowed mare sitting between them in the gap'; drove north, through the crossing and up the street.
He claims he was through Millhaven 'on market day' when it was 'well enough'; Sylvanas has just told him it has been dead five days; no one reconciles this.

Chapter 5 (Sylvanas's memory at the fork): the bench of old wagon boards with grain dust packed in the cracks recalls the carter's empty wagon ('Empty going up, full coming down', which she was pleased with herself for thinking at the Millhaven bridge), 'Nothing for me here, then' said plainly, and that he did not turn round but drove straight on north up the dead street 'as if he had business further up'. He asked after the young fellow with the cart. She tries him beside the depot and beside the cart man: he fits neither, 'except that he had asked after him.' 'An empty wagon, going the wrong way.' She wipes the dust off her nail and goes out.

Chapter 6: the farewell comes a second time, from a stranger. A granary tally-man on foot on the Andorhal road, having given directions to Captain Havel, says to Jaina as she passes: 'May the stars keep your road.' Ahead of her, Sylvanas turns in the saddle, all the way round, one hand on her horse's rump, to the road behind them: full, a carter cursing at a wheel in a rut, two women with baskets, pack mules. 'Mage. Did you read anything off him?' Jaina: 'Nothing but a tired clerk.' When they look back, the road is clear of anyone with a pale strap across his coat. He is gone.

Chapter 6: Sylvanas: 'The blessing. I had the same one at Millhaven, from an old carter going north over the bridge.' Jaina remembers a wagon on the bridge and voices, and nothing of what was said. Jaina: 'It's a farewell. Country people have dozens of them.' Sylvanas: 'Once, it's a farewell. Twice, it's wrong. That's as far as it goes yet.'

Chapter 6 guards held: Cyndia and Lyriel show no reaction or connection on the page. The man bears no resemblance to the carter (on foot; satchel with a pale strap; ink on a cuff). Jaina does not link him to the overseer; she has not turned the staff on him and half-asks herself whether she tried. He looked the four riders over and glanced back toward the granaries as he answered, which reads as a man sizing up armed strangers.

readerKnows_chapter6: The same blessing from two apparently unconnected strangers on two roads; Sylvanas says twice is wrong but not yet a pattern; Jaina's sense gave nothing.
povCharacterKnows_chapter6: Jaina (POV): a clerk's courtesy and a worried Sylvanas; no memory of the Millhaven words. Sylvanas: twice, no pattern yet. Cyndia and Lyriel: on page, nothing.
readerKnows_chapter5: Sylvanas now carries the carter as a nagging, unmatched item (the plan's chapter-end instruction); the prose still offers no proof.
readerKnows: An odd blessing, a noticed glance and a timeline snag.
povCharacterKnows: Sylvanas: marks it as odd and puts no weight on it. Cyndia heard it and reacted physically.
notes: Observable-only plant. No narration of intent. Do not make Sylvanas suspicious yet. Plan notes (not on page): Cyndia is an independent corroborating witness later; the spacing he sees (Cyndia left, Lyriel right, mage between) is the order of march for later chapters. Wording is fixed: 'May the stars keep your road.'
